group_structure.summary: Ownership sits above the restricted group: Funds managed by Fortress and Management jointly own Punch Taverns Limited (unrestricted Topco). Punch Taverns Limited owns Punch Pubs Group Limited (Parent Guarantor), which marks the top of the restricted group (dashed boundary on 9fin org chart). Punch Pubs Group Limited owns both Punch Finance plc (the Issuer of the £640m and £50m Senior Secured Notes) and Punch Pubs Holdings Limited (the 'Company', borrower under the £85m Super Senior RCF). Punch Pubs Holdings Limited sits above the four operating subsidiaries: Punch Partnerships (PML) Limited, Punch Taverns (Branston) Limited, and The Laine Pub Company Limited (all Guarantors, shaded on the chart), plus a bucket of Non-Guarantor Subsidiaries. The Laine Pub Company Limited has its own further Non-Guarantor Subsidiaries beneath it. All Guarantor entities, plus Punch Pubs Group Limited, Punch Pubs Holdings Limited and Punch Finance plc, sit inside the restricted group.
group_structure.restricted_group_note: Per the 9fin Bond Legal QuickTake on the £640m notes (20-May-2025), as of the 52 weeks ended 11-Aug-2024 the Issuer and Guarantors represented 97.7% of Group revenue, 98.5% of Adjusted Underlying EBITDA, and 92.9% of total assets -- i.e. the bulk of the freehold property base sits within the guarantor/collateral group, though not all of it. 9fin's own commentary flags a structural risk: the covenants permit the Issuer/Guarantors to transfer assets (including Collateral, i.e. freehold property) to non-Guarantor Restricted Subsidiaries, and there is no non-guarantor sub-limit for Ratio Debt, so structural subordination risk is 'heightened' in 9fin's assessment.
group_structure.property_owning_entities: The org chart does not break out a separate property-owning SPV or PropCo -- freehold and leasehold real estate is held directly within the operating Guarantor subsidiaries (Punch Partnerships (PML) Limited, Punch Taverns (Branston) Limited, The Laine Pub Company Limited) rather than ring-fenced in a dedicated real estate entity, based on the org chart and security package description. This differs from some UK pub/leisure structures (e.g. securitised propco/opco splits) and means property and trading risk sit in the same restricted entities.

debt_holdings.concentration_commentary: Holder base is granular: the top 10 lenders/funds hold only ~38% of the tranche between them, with 33 further holders (43 found in total) accounting for the remaining ~62%. The largest single holder, Fidelity, holds just 7.01%. Against the notes' amendment thresholds disclosed in 9fin's Bond Legal QuickTake (key money terms 90%, release of security 90%, release of guarantees 75%, other amendments 50.01%), no single holder or small handful of holders shown here appears close to a blocking or controlling stake -- consent solicitations would likely require broad syndication across many holders, which is a modestly credit-supportive feature (less concentration risk / single-holder leverage) but also means coordination in a restructuring scenario would involve a wide holder base.

property_freehold_analysis.estate_mix_ownership: Approximately 92% of Punch's ~1,264-1,298 pub sites are held freehold or long leasehold, with the remaining ~8% short leasehold (per Final Offering Memorandum, 21-May-2025, as of 23-Feb-2025 estate of 1,264 pubs). CEO commentary on the Q2 FY26 call (08-May-2026) reiterated 'the vast majority of our pubs are owned on a freehold basis' across an estate that had grown to 1,298 pubs by that date. Trend: freehold/long-leasehold ownership share has been broadly stable in the 92-96% range since at least 2021 (96% freehold cited in the 20-May-2025 9fin Credit QuickTake; 93% cited in 2021 QuickTakes), with bolt-on acquisitions (e.g. the 49 pubs acquired in FY26 for £42m) added on a freehold basis.
property_freehold_analysis.operating_model_mix: Two operating models: (1) Leased & Tenanted (L&T) -- publicans hold a lease/tenancy, pay Punch rent, and (under 'tie' arrangements covering ~97% of L&T pubs) commit to purchase the majority of drinks from Punch at above-market prices in exchange for below-market rent; and (2) Pub Partnership (PP, includes the Management Partnership/MP and Laine Pub Company sub-brands) -- Punch retains all sales and costs and pays the publican a percentage-based fee. As of the Feb-2025 OM, L&T was 75% of pubs (947 sites, ~60% of EBITDA) and PP was 25% (317 sites, ~40% of EBITDA before non-underlying items) -- PP is structurally higher-margin per site. By the Q2 FY26 call (08-May-2026), the mix had shifted to 922 L&T pubs (~71%) and 376 PP pubs (~29%) out of 1,298 total, consistent with management's stated strategy of converting L&T sites to PP (55 conversions in the prior 12 months referenced on the call; conversion economics historically ~£205k-230k capex per site for a ~33% ROI and ~93% uplift in outlet EBITDA per 9fin's 20-May-2025 Credit QuickTake).
property_freehold_analysis.freehold_valuation: Aggregate Property Value of GBP 1,079.4m as of the 17-May-2026 cap table date, per Savills valuation referenced explicitly by CFO Steve Dando on the Q2 FY26 earnings call (08-May-2026): 'secured against the Freehold pub estate, which was valued by Savills in 2025, and has a current property valuation of approximately £1.1 billion.' This is an independent third-party (Savills) valuation, not merely a book value. Historical valuation trend from 9fin sources: ~£849.7m (21-May-2021, 1,235 pubs) -> ~£879m (Dec-2021, at Fortress's acquisition of Punch from Patron Capital for an EV of ~£1bn) -> £992.0m (23-Feb-2025, per Final OM, 1,264 pubs) -> £1,079.4m (17-May-2026 cap table). The rise from £992m to £1,079.4m (+8.8%) over roughly 15 months reflects both bolt-on freehold acquisitions (e.g. the £42m/49-pub deal funded by the Feb-2026 tap) and underlying revaluation.
property_freehold_analysis.security_and_ltv: The £85m Super Senior RCF and £640m/£50m Senior Secured Notes are secured on a shared collateral package, including (per the 20-May-2025 9fin Bond Legal QuickTake on the notes) 'a fixed first equitable charge over all freehold property and certain leasehold real property (excluding leasehold real property that has 25 years or less to run or has rack-rent payable)', alongside share pledges, structural intercompany loan security, material bank accounts, and a floating charge over substantially all other assets. Notably, no legal mortgages are granted and there is no requirement to register/perfect the equitable charge (beyond debenture registration at Companies House) unless an acceleration event is ongoing -- a lighter-touch security package than a fully perfected legal mortgage, common in UK sponsor-backed HY structures but worth flagging as a practical recovery consideration. The 9fin cap table computes an explicit '% LTV' column defined as debt divided by Aggregate Property Value: Gross Secured Debt (£690.0m) / Aggregate Property Value (£1,079.4m) = 63.92% LTV; Net Secured Debt (£677.4m) / Property Value = 62.76% LTV; Gross Debt including leases (£761.9m) / Property Value = 70.59%; Net Debt (£749.3m) / Property Value = 69.42%. This LTV framing (property-value-based, not EBITDA-based) is 9fin's standard presentation for this credit and mirrors how UK pub-sector secured lending is typically underwritten.
property_freehold_analysis.ltv_covenant_status: The RCF carries a springing covenant requiring the LTV ratio of net cash RCF drawings to remain below 0.15, tested only at quarter-end if drawings exceed 40% of total commitments (per cap table note 1). This is narrower than a portfolio-wide maintenance LTV covenant on the bonds -- the debt instruments & covenants table for the £640m/£50m notes shows incurrence-based leverage tests (SSNL < 6.5x for the notes covenant basket, FCCR > 2x, and a TNL < 5.5x builder-basket condition, plus TNL < 6.4x one-time portability threshold) rather than a distinct property-LTV maintenance covenant. In short: freehold value underpins the security package and is disclosed prominently, but is not itself a tested maintenance covenant on the notes as far as 9fin's covenant data shows.
property_freehold_analysis.valuation_floor_vs_net_debt: On a straight book/independent-valuation basis, Aggregate Property Value of £1,079.4m provides asset coverage of approximately 1.42x Gross Debt (£761.9m, including leases) and 1.44x Net Debt (£749.3m) -- i.e. roughly £318-330m of headroom between the Savills freehold valuation and the group's all-in debt quantum. This is a materially different (and more supportive) picture than the 7.27x net-debt/EBITDA multiple would suggest in isolation, and is the basis for treating freehold real estate as a distinct hard-asset valuation floor / downside recovery reference point separate from the going-concern EBITDA multiple valuation. Caveat: this is a going-concern, largely desktop-style independent valuation (Savills), not a forced-sale or liquidation value. A 2021-era 9fin risk-factor extract on this same estate noted that 'Savills Valuation Report says the freehold and leasehold properties evaluation was done with limited due diligence and property inspections. Instead Savills valued the majority of properties on a desktop basis that contained a number of assumptions,' and separately that properties are 'revalued annually on a five-year rolling basis' with the majority assessed by the director supported by independent valuation of only a subset in a given year. In a genuine distressed/restructuring scenario, illiquidity in UK pub real estate, use-restriction covenants on some sites (limiting alcohol sale or requiring residential-only use), and the risk of a wave of independent-pub disposals depressing comparable values could all compress realisable value well below the £1.1bn headline figure. This valuation-methodology caveat is a real constraint on how much weight to place on the asset-coverage math above.
